points.description: States that a doubly-linked list needs extra memory/space, because each node must store an additional (back/previous) pointer.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if it says it uses more memory but does not link it to the extra pointer, or mentions the extra pointer without saying it costs space.

points.description: Identifies the extra space as being for the back (previous) pointers stored in each node.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a doubly-linked list uses extra space/memory for the back (previous) pointer in each node, in any wording. Part marks for a vague statement such as "uses more memory" without the pointer reason, or a correct answer mixed with a minor error. No marks for answers about other drawbacks (e.g. slower, more complex) that do not mention extra space.
